subject: science
passage: Most planetary scientists accept that the Moon formed about 4.5 billion years ago, when an object roughly the size of Mars, often called Theia, struck the young Earth. In the standard version of this "giant impact" model, most of the debris that later gathered into the Moon came from Theia rather than from Earth.
passage_b: Rocks brought back by the Apollo astronauts complicate that picture. The Moon's rocks turn out to be nearly identical to Earth's in their mix of oxygen isotopes, a chemical fingerprint that usually differs between bodies that formed in different parts of the solar system. Geochemist Lucía Ferrer argues that the collision must have been violent enough to mix material from both bodies thoroughly, or else that the Moon was built mostly from Earth itself.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the standard version of the giant impact model in Text 1?

choices.A: By claiming that the Apollo rocks show the Moon to be older than Earth
choices.B: By rejecting the idea that a collision with another body led to the Moon's formation
choices.C: By questioning where the Moon's material came from while accepting that an impact occurred
choices.D: By arguing that Theia formed in the same part of the solar system as Earth

explanation.why: Text 1's standard model says most of the Moon's material came "from Theia rather than from Earth." Text 2 says matching oxygen isotopes "complicate that picture," and Ferrer proposes that the material was thoroughly mixed or came "mostly from Earth." Both of her explanations still involve the collision, so Text 2 challenges only the source of the Moon's material.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 compares the chemistry of Earth and Moon rocks, not their ages.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Ferrer's explanations still assume "the collision" happened; Text 2 questions the details, not the impact itself.
explanation.C: Correct. Text 2 accepts that a collision occurred but doubts that the Moon is made mostly of Theia's material.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 never says where Theia formed. It notes that bodies from different regions usually have different isotopes, but it does not use this to place Theia near Earth.
